title: VPC + On‑Prem Ops: weekly deep‑dive and war‑room notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick sync notes from this week’s private deployments deep dive; capture recurring customer blockers across VPC and on‑prem installs, short mitigation experiments, and owners for follow‑ups. Not a polished runbook yet — working journal for the install squad and SRE pairing.

Attendees:
- Marcus Chen (owner)
- Aisha Hassan (network lead)
- Diego Alvarez (install engineer)
- Priya Rao (field SE)
- Leah Kim (SRE oncall)
- Joined for segment: Northstar Health success manager (30m)

High-level observations (summary):
- Two recurring failure modes this week: MTU blackhole on edge routers (intermittent TCP resets) and our config agent crashing during large KV imports. Both surface as "slow start" followed by partial node drift; customers see 5–20s spike then timeouts on multi‑token generation.
- Most new installs succeed; the failures cluster on older Juniper/Arista gear and closed corporate NATs with asymmetric routing.
- Customer impact: one escalated P1 (Northstar Health), four P2s with degraded throughput.

Standup updates (brief):
- Marcus: coordinated war‑room with Northstar; escalated to networking team at 2pm; drafted quick mitigation (disable jumbo frames upstream) and fallback to cpu‑fallback pool.
- Aisha: reproducer for MTU issue in lab (Arista 7280) — seen when path MTU < application packet; pushing small MTU probe patch to agent.
- Diego: agent crash traced to kvimport job hitting an ordering bug under high parallelism; added a 200ms linear backoff to import worker as a quick mitigation.
- Priya: working handoff doc for customer-side firewall rules; found one site using port‑mirroring that breaks UDP hole punching for KV sync.
- Leah: instrumented longer traces in the 1.3.2 runtime build; will capture tcpdump+stacktrace for next triage window.

Customer specifics — Northstar Health (P1):
- Symptom: periodic 15–25s token generation timeouts for sequences >512 tokens. Error: grpc DEADLINE_EXCEEDED followed by transient reconnects.
- Root cause (current hypothesis): packet fragmentation on WAN (MTU mismatch) causing large gRPC frames to be reassembled and triggering retransmit storms; combined with heavy KV warmup causing CPU saturation on primary node.
- Temporary mitigations applied: lowered advertised MTU on on‑prem LB to 1400; forced KV import to sequential mode for Northstar namespace; applied cpu‑fallback policy for half of their traffic.
- Immediate effect: 60% reduction in timeouts in a 1‑hour window; still seeing occasional 6–8s spikes.
- Next: schedule onsite network engineer call (Jira PD-4892) and capture full pcap during a spike window.

Engineering experiments + telemetry notes:
- MTU probe patch (aisha/mtu-probe-v2): sends graded 1500→1400→1300 test frames before large frame transfer; lab shows consistent failure at 1420 threshold on one Arista box. Need to validate on customer gear.
- KV import backoff: introduced 200ms linear backoff; initial tests show imports complete with fewer crashes but total import time increases ~18%. We'll explore adaptive backoff next (start at 30ms, escalate).
- Runtime trace: Leah enabled extended logs for tokenization and grpc flush points; retention 6h to avoid disk blowout. Correlate traces with pcap to find exact retransmit window.

Open blockers (who/ETA):
- Network vendor firmware mismatch at Northstar (Aisha / 2 business days) — awaiting vendor confirmation on recommended MTU handling.
- Agent crash root fix (Diego / 4 days) — code branch for ordering guard in review (PR #274).
- Onsite time for customer firewall changes (Priya / customer scheduling) — tentative Monday window.
- Long‑term: graceful KV warmup (L2) + throttling in control plane (Marcus + Leah / sprint 48).

Short action items (this week):
- Aisha: push mtu‑probe to canary on staging, collect success/fail matrix across Arista/Juniper (due 2024‑07‑17).
- Diego: land ordering guard + add import job adaptive backoff experiment (due 2024‑07‑19).
- Priya: finalize firewall rule one‑pager and send to Northstar SM (due 2024‑07‑16).
- Leah: upload pcap sampling playbook to Confluence and add runbook pointer in PD-4892 (due 2024‑07‑18).
- Marcus: coordinate vendor call and update on customer slack channel; prepare executive one‑pager if issue persists past Friday.

Notes to self / loose thoughts (brainstorm):
- Could we default to gRPC streaming chunk sizes smaller on edge deployments? Low perf cost maybe but prevents fragmentation spikes.
- Consider automatic detection of MTU reassembly events via tcp info and flip to small‑chunk mode for that client.
- Add a telemetry metric: % of gRPC frames larger than X bytes resulting in retransmits — useful for routing rules.

Risks / escalation ladder:
- If MTU vendor fix takes >5 business days, escalate to platform infra for a temporary traffic‑split to our dedicated Hosted fallback for affected customers (contracts permitting).
- Communicate SLA implications to CS if spikes persist beyond 72 hours.

Meeting follow‑ups / next sync:
- War‑room check Tuesday 10:30am PT — focused on Northstar pcap and vendor feedback.
- Weekly deep‑dive next Friday 9am PT — demo of mtu‑probe canary results.

Appendix: useful commands and snippets (lab):
- tcpdump sample: sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/northstar_pcap.pcap 'tcp and host <customer_ip>'
- check TX/RX MTU mismatch: ip link show dev eth0 && ethtool -k eth0
- quick import backoff toggle (dev box): export KV_IMPORT_BACKOFF_MS=200 && ./kv-import --namespace northstar

Unresolved questions:
- Why do only some Juniper devices appear immune? firmware vs config? (Aisha to validate configs)
- Is chunked gRPC built for our current model sizes without regressions? (Perf team to sign off)

End notes: this doc is living — update with pcap links and final PR number once Diego lands the fix. Keep trace windows small and annotate with customer timestamps.
